Consonantal i

Theme

Latin word

alter

alter, altera, alterum

adjective and pronoun; gen. alterīus, dat. alterī

another, a second (like the first); the other (of two); repeated, the one … the other

In this lexicon

  • another

    also used · classical · Cic. Amic. 80: tamquam alter īdem; Cic. Sen. 56: succīdiam alteram

  • the other

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Att. 6.1.12: alter … frēnīs eget, alter calcāribus; Petr. 31.3: in alterā parte albās, in alterā nigrās

  • ūnus et alter: couple

    classical

  • alter alterum: each other

    classical

Examples

  • est enim is quī est tamquam alter īdem

    for a friend is, as it were, a second selfCic. Amic. 80

    In the entry for another

  • Cicerōnēs puerī amant inter sē, exercentur, sed discunt, alter … frēnīs eget, alter calcāribus

    the two Cicero boys are fond of each other, they take their exercise, and they learn too, but the one needs the reins, the other the spursCic. Att. 6.1.12

    In the entry for the other
